description:
The /fly HUD velocity readout displays 'NaN km/s' throughout the entire transit to any outer-planet destination (Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, Pluto, Ceres, Vesta, Psyche, Bennu). The same NaN propagates through the velocity-arrow length, the data-helio-kms DOM attribute, and the SpacecraftInfoCard speed row.

Expected: The HUD shows a physically meaningful positive speed in km/s at every spacecraft position. For a Hohmann transfer to Jupiter (a = (1.0 + 5.203)/2 = 3.102 AU), the speed at Earth departure follows the vis-viva equation: v = √(µ·(2/r − 1/a))·AU/yr→km/s ≈ 38.5 km/s. The speed monotonically decreases toward arrival at the destination. The value is always finite and positive.

Acceptance criteria:
- The HUD velocity readout must never display 'NaN km/s' for any mission or plan that /fly can load. `Number.isNaN(heliocentricKms)` must be false on every frame of every transit. [code-invariant: NaN in a user-facing display is a crash — no document needed.]
- The transfer semi-major axis `aTransferAu` passed to `flyHeliocentricSpeed()` in the `$derived` at line 952 must be derived from the actual destination's orbital radius, not hardcoded to Mars. Expected: `a = (R_EARTH_AU + DESTINATIONS[activeDestination].a) / 2` for non-Moon heliocentric missions. Both `DESTINATIONS` and `activeDestination` are already in scope at line 952. [repo-data: DESTINATIONS record at src/lib/lambert-grid.constants.ts:131-144 defines `.a` (semi-major axis) for every DestinationId. `activeDestination` is declared as `$state<DestinationId>('mars')` at fly/+page.svelte:300. Both are imported/in-scope at the `$derived` site at line 952.]
- The speed readout value must satisfy vis-viva bounds for the actual destination. For Jupiter at departure: `v = sqrt(4π² · (2/1.0 − 2/(1+5.203))) · 4.7404 ≈ 38.5 km/s`. For all destinations, the value must be finite and positive across the full [R_EARTH_AU, DESTINATIONS[id].a] distance range. [spec: ADR-030 §'Trajectory math' / fly-physics.ts:L39-41 — vis-viva is the canonical formula. The function itself is sound; the call site at fly/+page.svelte:952 feeds it the wrong transfer a.]

Domain facts:
- Jupiter semi-major axis: 5.203 AU (DESTINATIONS.jupiter.a via static/data/planets.json)
- Saturn semi-major axis: 9.537 AU
- Mars semi-major axis: 1.524 AU — the value currently hardcoded into the speed call site
- DESTINATIONS is imported at line 65 from $lib/lambert-grid.constants
- activeDestination is declared as $state<DestinationId>('mars') at line 300

Target: src/routes/fly/+page.svelte — line 952 `$derived` expression — the second argument (aTransferAu) of the `flyHeliocentricSpeed(scR, ...)` call. Replace the hardcoded `R_MARS_AU` with `DESTINATIONS[activeDestination].a` to compute the transfer semi-major axis from the actual destination: `(R_EARTH_AU + DESTINATIONS[activeDestination].a) / 2`.
Do NOT change DO NOT touch the HUD display markup (lines 6783, 6934, 5419, 6473) or the SpacecraftInfoCard component — they are passive consumers of the NaN. The fix is exclusively in the `$derived` computation at line 952. DO NOT add a `Number.isNaN` guard in the display layer — that masks the symptom without fixing the math. The `area: "ui"` routing from the previous pass was wrong; the correct area is `backend` (data computation in a `$derived` expression). The specialist's previous 14-turn grind on the UI markup of the same file is the decoy to avoid repeating. — it is not the owner of this symptom.
